title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 100-102). Grothendieck is analysing the boundary stratification of the Deligne-Mumford compactification of M_{g,nu}. Strata are indexed by stable 'graphs' (his word is hard to read, possibly 'm-graphes' or a similar term). For a stable graph G, M_G is the modular multiplicity (stack) of stable curves of combinatorial type G. Here the type is apparently rigidified, i.e. the dual graph is identified with G.

A 'morphisme de normalisation' G' -> G is a partial normalisation: G' is obtained by cutting some edges of G into pairs of half-edges, with the induced map of graphs. Base change compatibility of the corresponding operation on curves gives a contravariant morphism M_G -> M_{G'}.

The previous page proves two things:
(a) For a strict normalisation morphism, M_G -> M_{G'} is an isomorphism.
(b) M of a disjoint sum is the product of the M's.

On this page these facts are transported to fundamental groupoids:
- Pi_1 M_G is a contravariant functor in G for normalisation morphisms.
- It sends strict normalisation morphisms to equivalences of groupoids.
- It sends sums of stable graphs to products of groupoids.

The key consequence is formula (144). Take the minimal strict sub-object, i.e. the full normalisation G~: cut every edge, leaving the disjoint union of the vertices alpha in S, each with genus g_alpha and its set Î_alpha of half-edges plus marked points. This gives Pi_1 M_G ≃ ∏_{alpha in S} Pi_1 M_{g_alpha, Î_alpha}. In modern terms, the rigidified boundary stratum is the product of smaller open moduli stacks, so its fundamental groupoid is the product of the profinite or discrete mapping-class groupoids of the vertex surfaces.

The square (145) records a criterion. Each G has a tautological normalisation G~ -> G, and G' -> G is strict if and only if the induced map G~' -> G~ is an isomorphism. This automatically recovers the equivalences Pi_1 M_{G'} -> Pi_1 M_G.

Purpose. The next page reduces arbitrary normalisation ('modulation') morphisms between strata to the forgetful maps Pi_1 M_{g,I} -> Pi_1 M_{g,I'} for I' ⊂ I. This is the combinatorial skeleton of the 'Teichmüller tower' and the two-level principle of the Esquisse d'un programme: boundary strata, and the tubular neighbourhoods at infinity, are controlled by the groupoids of the M_{g,n} for small (g,n) and the point-forgetting maps between them.
errors: The product formula (144) holds only for the graph-rigidified stratum (curves with dual graph identified with G). For the unrigidified stratum one gets a quotient [∏ M_{g_v,n_v}/Aut(G)], and Pi_1 is an extension by Aut(G). The text implicitly works with rigidified objects; this is not an error if M_G is defined that way.
The notation alternates between Pi M_G and Pi_1 M_G. The final ')' in (144) is a stray parenthesis. Neither is substantive.

ideas.what: Boundary strata of M̄_{g,n} indexed by stable graphs are products of smaller open moduli stacks M_{g_v,n_v}, obtained by normalising the nodal curve.
ideas.modern_name: Clutching/gluing morphisms; stratification of M̄_{g,n} by stable graphs
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne-Mumford (1969), Knudsen (1983); stable graph formalism standard since the 1990s (e.g. Kontsevich-Manin, Getzler-Kapranov)
ideas.where_published: Implicit in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), section on the Teichmüller tower and 'structure à l'infini'

ideas.what: Functoriality of the fundamental groupoids of strata under partial normalisation of graphs: strict normalisations give equivalences, and sums of graphs go to products of groupoids.
ideas.modern_name: Modular-operad/graph-category functoriality of strata; mapping class groupoid of the boundary
ideas.usually_credited_to: Getzler-Kapranov (modular operads, 1998); work of Hatcher-Lochak-Schneps and Nakamura on the Teichmüller tower

ideas.what: Reduction of all boundary 'modulation' morphisms to point-forgetting maps Pi_1 M_{g,I} -> Pi_1 M_{g,I'} (continued on the next page).
ideas.modern_name: Teichmüller tower / Birman-type forgetful maps; two-level principle
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse); developed by Lochak-Schneps, Hatcher-Lochak-Schneps, Nakamura

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard bookkeeping step: strata as products of smaller moduli stacks, and functoriality of their fundamental groupoids. It is consistent with what is known from the Esquisse and later Teichmüller-tower literature, and contains nothing that would surprise a specialist.
transcription_corrections: Line 3-4: 'et commute aux quotients[?] stables au produit des groupoïdes' should most likely read '... et transforme sommes de [graphes] stables en produit des groupoïdes correspondants'. 'sommes' is meant rather than 'quotients', matching part (b) of the previous page.
'qui tient compte des (et redonne entre-temps[?])' is probably 'qui tient compte des (et redonne automatiquement)'.
'(qui reviennent en effet des iso. pour les normalisés stricts G̃' et G̃ de G' is probably '(qui proviennent en effet des iso. pour les normalisés stricts G̃' de G' et G̃ de G)'.
Equation (144): the extra closing parenthesis is a stray mark; it reads Pi_1 M_G ≃ ∏_{alpha∈S} Pi_1 M_{g_alpha, Î_alpha}.
